title: Design the SLA Policy from Data
scenario: No policy is handed to you this time. Given last quarter's actual completion times, DESIGN the onboarding SLA policy: choose deadlines with enough margin that tasks finish on time, keep payroll earliest, and version it. The validator checks the shape and the ordering; the numbers are your call to defend.
input: Last quarter, measured in business days before start when each task actually finished: payroll typically cleared 3-4 days out (slowest, cycle-bound); accounts 2-3 days out; hardware 1-3 days out (variable, supply-dependent); access 1-2 days out. Design deadlines with margin so most runs finish on time. Constraints: every SLA is a positive integer number of business days before start, and payroll must remain the earliest (largest). Version the policy 2.0.0.
instructions: Choose each SLA as a positive integer of business days before start, with margin from the data.
Keep payroll the earliest: payrollSla must exceed accessSla.
Name the policy, set owner, and version it 2.0.0.
Return one JSON object, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Design an onboarding SLA policy from completion data: pick positive integer deadlines (business days before start) with margin, keep payroll the earliest (payrollSla > accessSla), owner People Ops Lead, version 2.0.0.
successMessage: SLA policy designed. Your deadlines have margin from real data, and payroll still leads.
editorHelper: Design the numbers - defend them with the data and the ordering.

sections.title: Policy is a judgement call
sections.body: An SLA is a promise the teams must keep. Set it too tight and every run breaches; too loose and there is no urgency. Design means choosing the margin the data justifies.

sections.title: Read the distribution, not the average
sections.body: Hardware finished 1-3 days out - so an SLA at its average would breach half the time. Good design leans toward the slow end so most runs finish on time.

sections.title: Constraints still bind
sections.body: Payroll stays earliest for the pay cycle. Design is freedom within constraints: your numbers can vary, but the ordering that encodes dependencies must hold.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: A versioned SLA policy you designed from evidence - the governed input every future plan applies.
